A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AlphaSAGE, with readable text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices. Retained content can be matched across appendix moves and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on CSI300, CSI500 and S&P500, including backtests, component ablations and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds CSI1000 evaluation, additional comparisons, diagnostic experiments, runtimes and five-seed summaries.

M1.justification: The RGCN encoder, GFlowNet objective, early stopping, reward components, entropy regularization and dynamic combiner are retained. Algorithm 1 is unchanged apart from references; alternative encoders and schedules are experimental comparisons, not revisions to the proposed method.

E1.justification: V3 adds CSI1000 as another Chinese equity universe in Table 1, retaining the original markets and alpha-mining/backtesting tasks. Appendix E.8 discusses existing evaluation windows rather than introducing a new evaluated regime scenario.

E2.justification: V3 adds the LLM-based AlphaAgent to the main comparisons on all retained universes. Tables 9–10 also introduce a Transformer encoder comparator and an RL configuration augmented with the proposed structural components, substantially expanding the comparisons used to assess AlphaSAGE's advantages.

E3.justification: The retained benchmarks keep their stated splits, metrics, portfolio rules and default settings. V3 adds protocols varying maximum expression length, encoder depth, hidden dimension and reward schedules, alongside a similar-parameter-budget Transformer comparison and crossed RL/GFlowNet component controls.

E4.justification: V3 retains the original ablations and sensitivity plots, then adds expression-length, encoder-depth, hidden-size and reward-schedule studies, encoder comparisons, framework/component disentanglement and runtime analysis in Appendix E.2–E.6. The regime discussion in E.8 supplies interpretation, not additional subperiod-test results.

E5.justification: V1 lacks explicit repeated-run counts and uncertainty summaries. V3 Appendix E.7/Table 12 reports means and standard deviations over five seeds for AlphaGen, AlphaQCM, AlphaForge and AlphaSAGE on CSI300. This is newly documented uncertainty, not evidence of an increase from a previously specified run count.

E6.justification: The original Table 1 entries and Table 2 are numerically unchanged. V3 adds AlphaAgent/CSI1000 outcomes and extensive diagnostic, runtime and repeated-run results. New comparisons include AlphaAgent exceeding AlphaSAGE on CSI500 ICIR, 0.396 versus 0.379, and AlphaQCM exceeding it on CSI1000 RIC, 0.107 versus 0.096.

T1.justification: The diversity proposition, proof and ridge corollary are unchanged, moving from Appendix E to F. The added standard portfolio-return formula in Section 2.1 explains existing financial concepts rather than introducing new theoretical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same three-part framework and broad claims of diverse, predictive alphas and superior cross-market portfolio performance. The additional experiments do not redefine the central contribution.

C2.justification: V3 adds substantive explanations of reward compatibility, capacity and scheduling tradeoffs, computational overhead and the distinction between IC and realized returns. Appendix E.8 explicitly qualifies short-window return dominance under market shocks, adding applicability limits absent from v1's discussion.

D1.justification: V3 newly discloses baseline repository pointers and default-setting instructions in D.3, plus caching details and training times in E.6. The original pseudocode, relation types, feature/operator inventory, default hyperparameters and AlphaSAGE code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: The reference lists and existing literature survey are unchanged. V3 gives the already-cited AlphaAgent an explicit role as an LLM comparator and adds a description of its multi-agent workflow, modestly extending comparative positioning.

P1.justification: V3 adds a finance-background subsection and targeted explanatory passages, edits citation and author/header presentation, and reorders the implementation, experiment, results and proof appendices. Most original prose and the main narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains dataset and comparator rows, Figure 3 gains an AlphaAgent curve and revised legend, and Tables 5–12 add several distinct analytical displays. Existing figures and tables are relocated, Figure 2 receives a revised caption, and Table 13 redisplays selected CSI300 results rather than new evidence.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens experimental attribution and reliability: the similar-budget Transformer comparison and RL/component controls address alternatives unresolved by v1's ablations, while five-seed summaries quantify previously unreported variability. These gains outweigh reporting defects, including the retained all-correlation-metrics superiority claim contradicted by Table 1 and Table 13's repetition of CSI300 results without a new subperiod analysis.
